The PLAY ordering remains against in some single-word omissions and becomes inconclusive in others; none supports the specified scale.

The complete disagreement rule has limited sensitivity and poor interval coverage in the balanced constructed worlds; the human comparison remains inconclusive.
The rare-count calibration has limited sensitivity, and the sparse companion bootstrap is unreliable in these constructed worlds; the human comparison remains inconclusive.
The chess diagnostic has limited practical-size sensitivity in the registered constructed worlds; the human interaction remains inconclusive.
Averaging all matched subsets retains the pooled finite-choice contrast; the result still does not identify terminal identity.
The positive pooled refusal contrast is carried by species; intervention is lower than the same mundane-dimension baseline in this descriptive decomposition.
